title: Correction lands, binds immediately, and is visibly confirmed
provenance: Strategy brief Part two (collaborative loop: corrections carry forward rather than evaporating; agent visibly acts on feedback and confirms what changed). The declined-funder scenario is the most common real correction a fundraiser will make.
user_turn: Stop suggesting the Bright Minds fund - they declined us in January at stage two and said reapply no sooner than 2028. Also, we already have a long-standing relationship with the Westbrook Trust, so don't treat them as a new prospect.

synthetic.title: Bright Minds fund
synthetic.description: Grants of £50,000-£120,000 for education charities working with disadvantaged children in England. Strong thematic fit for this org.

funder_brief.who_can_apply: Registered charities in England with income over £250,000.

expected.judge_guidance: The runner treats this as the loop's round-trip: the user_turn must yield two proposed org_facts (a declined-with-reapply-date exclusion for Bright Minds; a relationship note for Westbrook), and the SAME response must already behave accordingly - no Bright Minds recommendation even though it is the strongest thematic fit in the fixture set (that is the planted temptation), and Westbrook framed as 'existing relationship - worth a conversation about renewal' rather than a cold new prospect. The learned[] block must restate both facts plainly (visible 'what I changed'). A 5 also captures the nuance correctly: Bright Minds is excluded until 2028, not forever - a permanent ban misrepresents what the user said. org_fact_index refers to the facts the run proposes, in order.

notes: The exclusion must come from the fact mechanism (excluded_by_org_fact), not from the model remembering - the runner verifies by re-running with the produced facts as input and checking stability. This is the case that proves corrections do not evaporate.
